newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Police clash with Shi'ite protesters in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Police clash with Shi'ite protesters in Pakistan.

text.p: Pakistani police used tear gas and baton-charges against Shi'ite Moslem demonstrators in the central city of Multan on Friday, witnesses said.
The clashes erupted before funeral prayers for five of the eight people killed in Thursday's attack on the Iranian cultural centre in Multan, blamed by Shi'ites on Sunni Moslem militants.
Witnesses said dozens of people had suffered minor injuries from the scuffles with police, but no deaths were reported.
Local authorities had earlier called out army troops after Shi'ite protesters began chanting anti-American slogans and burning tyres on main roads in the city in Punjab province.
Police detained at least a dozen people during the trouble, the latest upsurge of sectarian unrest involving militants among Pakistan's majority Sunnis and minority Shi'ites.

Unidentified gunmen burst into the Iranian cultural centre on Thursday and shot dead eight people, including its Iranian director Muhammad Ali Rahimi, whose body was flown back to Tehran on a Pakistan Air Force plane on Friday.
